execution.ref: claude/a4-admission-controllers from origin/main 32e79ffb0 (A4-DEDICATED-ADMISSION-CONTROLLERS-01, Test Lead ruling on readiness item A4)
execution.description: Built #615's recorded follow-up: zero-spend grants refused by every spending path, `phase3 admission-controller init` that creates a dedicated controller store and prints its identity, one pending Level 0 designation per Challenge (battery, cooling, motor), and readiness item A4 wired to the designation file.

expected: Each Challenge's admission state lives in its own controller with a fixed identity, created offline with no spend, and A4 passes only once that identity is designated.
observed: The recorded follow-up could not be run: no command created a controller store, and the grant format could not express zero spend (a positive run cost and at least one run were required). A4 still carried the stale reason '#615 not on main' and checked nothing. Making zero spend a whole shape (every amount 0, 0 runs, 0 submissions) and refusing it at each spending entry point kept every existing grant unchanged. A zero-spend grant file still binds spend authority, so it needs the owner's own approval even at USD 0.
keep: A recorded follow-up is not done until the operator command it needs exists on main; check the command before ruling an item ready for the executor.
A no-spend authority is a whole, explicit shape refused at every spending entry point, never a convention of small values.
A readiness item reads the record it names (here the designation file), so a pending identity FAILs (a LOCK is refused until it is recorded) and so does a malformed record.
change: With the three owner-approved zero-spend admission grants committed, run `admission-controller init` per Challenge on the operator host, and fill the identities in a one-line follow-up.
Consume battery Level 0 findings already on the R2 root (#609) into the dedicated controller before any battery Level 0 LOCK review.
